text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Senior Minister Lee Kuan Yew tells High Court opposition politician Tang Liang Hong gets backing from someone or some agency to maximise political damage to Singapore, as court allows deletion of Lee's offending remarks on Johor from record.
- Lee says his remarks on Johor not deemed newsworthy until Malaysian lawyer Abdul Razak highlights to media.
- Every child in Singapore to get hands-on use of computers when government implements six-year information technology master plan costing Singapore $2 billion.
- Singapore Telecommunication share prices plunge, causing key Straits Times Index for the bourse to drop below 2,000 points for first time in two years.
- Average values of resale Housing Board flats in 13 housing estates fall between 0.2 and 2.5 percent in first quarter from previous quarter.
- Rumours about government announcing further measures tightening public housing loans hit property stocks and stock exchange property index plunges 2.4 percent or 16 points to 657.04.
- Senior finance officials of G-7 express concern further weakening of yen may ignite new trade tensions between United States and Japan.
- Stock Exchange of Singapore plans to conduct own investigation on allegations of insider trading by Lum Chang Group and NOL.
- Forecast by economists show a slow GDP growth of 3.7 percent in first quarter due to contraction in manufacturing output.
- Bankers and analysts forsee further fall in IPO pricing with stock market flailing and public float fever cooling.
- Hongkong-based Thakral Corporation moves closer to Singapore dollar listing by relocating its treasury operations, incurring more than a third of its expenses in Singapore.
- San Teh plans to raise US $20 million for new plant through bond issue and share placement.
- Sin Soon Huat shares hit low of 73 cents amid rumours that its controlling shareholder is selling substantial stake.
- Creative Technology stocks jump 5.9 percent to Singapore $21.50 apiece on renewed optimism about company's future performance, and analysts forecaste further rise.
